newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez denies Jassan charge - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez denies Jassan charge - paper.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez denied that he had asked Justice Minister Elias Jassan to intercede with a judge in 1994, according to a newspaper interview Friday.
Jassan said on television Monday that Fernandez approached him in October 1994 and asked him to influence a judge on behalf of then-Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.
But Fernandez told the Clarin newspaper that he had only informed Jassan that Cavallo was furious about a judge's investigation into alleged corruption charges against him.

Fernandez said Cavallo telephoned him and told him he would accuse the government of using the probe to damage him politically if the judge called him to testify and prevented him making a trip abroad he was planning.

"What Cavallo told me is that if they forced him to give evidence at that date he would call a press conference to say that the government wanted to manipulate the investigation," Fernandez told Clarin in Asuncion, where he was attending a meeting of the Mercosur customs union.

Fernandez went on, "I thought about it at length and decided I should pass the matter to the Justice Minister because the problem entered into his area. So I told Minister Jassan that Cavallo had called me and was worried because he had to travel and the summons was stopping him traveling."
Fernandez said that he left the matter in Jassan's hands and that he did not know what happened next.
Cavallo denied Jassan's charges in a press conference Monday.
Cavallo, the architect of Argentina's currency board system which has given the country one of the world's lowest inflation rates, was fired as economy minister by President Carlos Menem a year ago.

Cavallo then launched himself as a new opposition force to the governing Peronist Party and has accused Jassan and Interior Minister Carlos Corach of manipulating judges. Both ministers have denied the charges.
